title: Tame invariants commute with arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $G$ a finite group of order $d$ with $d\in A^\times$, and $M$ an $A$-module with an $A$-linear $G$-action. Write $M^G=\{m:g(m)=m\text{ for every }g\in G\}$. The $A$-linear operator $e_M=d^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}g$ is idempotent, has image $M^G$, and restricts to the identity on $M^G$. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$, the natural map
$$B\otimes_A M^G\longrightarrow(B\otimes_A M)^G$$
is an isomorphism of $B$-modules, with $G$ acting trivially on $B$. It is natural in equivariant module maps and in $B$. If $M=C$ is a commutative $A$-algebra on which $G$ acts by $A$-algebra automorphisms, this comparison is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras
$$B\otimes_A C^G\simeq(B\otimes_A C)^G.$$
Neither $B$ nor $C$ is required to be flat over $A$. Tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].
